Reflections from Esri UC 2026: AI, GIS, and the Future of Mining

2026-07-22 Esri Blog Esri UC 2026, AI, GIS, mining, GeoAI, digital twin, Jack Dangermond, deep learning, reclamation, environmental monitoring, 3D visualization
Read the source article

Quick summary

Esri UC 2026 showcased how AI and GIS are converging in the mining industry, with Jack Dangermond declaring "GIS is a Digital Twin," and companies demonstrating GeoAI-powered reclamation workflows, VR-enabled mining operations, and community engagement through geospatial platforms.

Key takeaways

  • Jack Dangermond's central message was that "GIS enables AI and AI enhances GIS," with the GIS community shifting from AI experimentation to real implementation
  • Data readiness—cleanup, governance, integration, and standardization—remains the largest hurdle for mining companies seeking to implement AI, with poor inputs still producing poor outputs
  • Stantec demonstrated GeoAI deep learning models automating tree counts for bond release and monitoring landslide conditions with greater consistency than manual sampling
  • Teck's MetaTwin platform combines geoscience data, engineering models, sensors, drone imagery, and GIS into a VR-enabled environment for planning, permitting, training, and stakeholder engagement
  • A dedicated Esri Mining User Group webpage was launched to connect GIS professionals across the mining industry with newsletters, customer spotlights, and community-driven content
